articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed; 11/12/13/15/15 stories selected; avg 12 published per cycle; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05) bars a new one; nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: Multi-source is 25% against 30% (16 of 63), up from 20% yesterday. The feed was thin on multi-source stories: the 10:00 selector found only 4, and economy's multi-source floor went unmet in three of five cycles because the candidates were market recaps without a cause or repeats of the morning's US inflation story.
watching: Gulf war: a container ship sank in Hormuz, the war reached Saudi Arabia's Dhahran oil heartland, and analysts say Riyadh's containment strategy has collapsed.
Ukraine: SpaceX throttled Starlink over Ukraine, Musk blamed Washington for Starshield limits, and Zelensky said he feels betrayed by Trump.
Black Sea: Germany urged a shipping ceasefire after attacks threatened grain flows to Africa.
Ebola: Kenya confirmed a second case as the DR Congo toll climbs.
Horn of Africa: Ethiopia and Eritrea traded Article 51 letters at the UN, and Egypt and Sudan plan a Halayeb border pact.
Nord Stream: the sabotage trial opened in Hamburg.
Press freedom: Turkish police raided Halk TV, Russia charged a Japanese reporter, and Pakistan banned live coverage of attacks.
Economy: US inflation rose on gasoline, the IMF warned of fiscal limits and a debt squeeze, and China's exports rose 36%.
AI and chips: Google halved Gemini prices, ASML's China sales doubled, and Nvidia's China share fell.
coverageGaps: Oceania had no datelines today, after one yesterday.
Science leaned on Ebola and climate stories; three cycles reported the feed had no Quanta, New Scientist or Carbon Brief findings, though the day still reached 10.
Five stories rest only on state or advocacy sources (Black Sea shipping, Costa Rica prisons, Ethiopia-Eritrea letters, Nord Stream trial, Sberbank strike), up from four.
context: Every target but multi-source is met: Latin America rose to 8% (Mexico City twice, Goiás, Salvador, San José) from 3%, and US datelines held at 24%. Al Jazeera's share of 19% is one article under the 20% cap, worth watching. Cycles averaged 959s with all five completing.
